items.stem: Why use a structured interview with a fixed question set?

options.text: It makes candidates comparable and reduces bias
options.rationale: Correct: consistent, job-relevant questions improve fairness and comparability.

options.text: It guarantees the best hire every time
options.rationale: Structure improves fairness but cannot guarantee outcomes.

options.text: It removes the need for human judgement
options.rationale: Humans still make and own the decision.

options.text: It is faster to skip criteria
options.rationale: Skipping criteria undermines the purpose of structure.

items.explanation: Correct: consistent, job-relevant questions improve fairness and comparability.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An AI screening tool is described as 'unbiased'. What is the correct stance?

options.text: Review it for bias; AI can reflect biased data
options.rationale: Correct: AI can inherit and amplify bias, so human review and fairness checks are required.

options.text: Trust the claim and skip review
options.rationale: Accepting an unverified fairness claim is risky.

options.text: Use it only for protected groups
options.rationale: That would itself be discriminatory and improper.

options.text: Let it make the final decision

items.explanation: Correct: AI can inherit and amplify bias, so human review and fairness checks are required.

items.stem: Which TWO support a fair, defensible hiring process? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: predefined criteria make decisions evidence-based.

options.text: Documenting the evidence behind each rating
options.rationale: Correct: documentation makes the decision defensible.

items.explanation: Correct: predefined criteria make decisions evidence-based.
